text:
Marcus Pettersson was never brought to New York for his offense. The tall Swede from Skellefteå, who spent most of his career in Pittsburgh (442 games) before a stop in Vancouver, plays almost 21 minutes a night for the Rangers and has three assists and 30 blocked shots in 18 games.

The job is the chances against. Evolving-Hockey rated him one of the best at taking them away last season: after adjusting for teammates and opponents, the other team got 0.23 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there, a 98th-percentile mark, while his teammates sat in the bottom 3% by their impact. The flip side is just as stark: his team created almost nothing with him on, bottom 5% of defensemen.

This season the Rangers have broken even on expected goals (the quality of chances) with him at five on five, about 51%, and they've scored a little more than that with him on the ice. We'd judge him on whether the chances against stay down when he's out there, not on his point total, which our numbers put around 18 the rest of the way.
headline: Marcus Pettersson is the Rangers' quiet stopper
